The template count in `test_queries.py` is 16 and the universe size in `test_query_probes.py` at least 125. `tests/support/predicate_removal.py::mutant_of` registers the copy of a template instance under the template's id, because the registry refuses a colon in a statement id; the predicate-removal check of the generated test now runs over the sixteen templates, and a statement that anchored a child with a `WHERE c.tenantId = $tenant` outside the map form survived it, so those anchors are written `(c {tenantId: $tenant} WHERE ...)`.
10. **What this does not do.** (a) `Q-RES-MERGE-RELS` is label-less and anchored: its endpoints are of every kind (root, child, version, shared), no index backs a child or version key, and its database hits grow with the graph (247, 840 and 3,480 per row at 1, 10 and 50 tenants). It is no worse than before and is not asserted; an index per child label (a later migration) or a typed split by endpoint kind is the fix (known-issues). (b) The schema keeps the single-property keys `resource_id`, `concept_key` and `identifier_key` until TEN-032, so on the production schema a second tenant that writes a resource id, a concept or an identifier the first holds meets a unique-constraint failure and gets `Conflict`; the isolation and two-tenant tests run on the contracted schema (DEC-159). (c) The statements of other repositories that create or match `Resource`, `Concept` or `Identifier` nodes without the tenant (`Q-COMM-ADD`, `Q-ROLE-CHANNEL`, `Q-PROV-LINK` and the others on the ratchet) still write unstamped nodes the store will not see; they convert in TEN-010 to TEN-017. (d) Nothing runs `invariant_violations` yet (TEN-031).
11. **A reference or a resource type must be a plain resource-type name that no other statement reads (round 2).** A reference makes a placeholder labelled with its type, so a reference to `Tenant/x` made a `Resource:Tenant` node that the global statements of TEN-007 (which match the registry labels with no tenant bound) could read. `put` now refuses, before any write and with `ValidationFailed` that repeats nothing of the value, a reference whose type is not letters only with a capital first letter, or is one of the registry labels (`REGISTRY_LABELS` of `migrations_tenant.py`, `GLOBAL_STATEMENT_LABELS` of `queries.py`, not copied) or one of the store's own labels (`Resource`, `ResourceVersion`, `ResourceVersionPart`, `Concept`, `CodeSystem`, `Identifier`); the same set is refused as the type of the resource itself. Tests: `test_a_reference_to_a_registry_label_or_a_non_type_is_refused_and_writes_nothing` (13 targets, a single reference and a list), `test_a_resource_of_a_registry_type_is_refused_and_writes_nothing`, `test_a_reference_to_an_ordinary_type_is_still_accepted`.

## DEC-165 The inbound queue consumers (I08): the tenant is bound from the message, the reply processor holds no unit of work around its use case, a delivery status only moves forward, and the choices the prompt leaves open
Status: accepted (builder build-I08, under DEC-133) · Affects: `adapters/inbound/workers/reply_processor.py`, `delivery_tracker.py`, `tenant_binding.py` (new), `consumer.py` (`MessageConsumer`), `servicebus_runner.py` (reads `tenantId`, `serve`), `bootstrap/workers_main.py` (new), `application/ports/outbound/idempotency.py` (`ProcessedMessages.seen`), `messaging.py` (`statuses_before`), `graph_store/idempotency_store.py` (`Q-PROCESSED-SEEN`), `graph_store/communication_repository.py` (`Q-COMM-SET-STATUS`), `graph_store/connection.py` (`Neo4jConnection.driver`), the `BINDING_MODULES` pin, I04 and I05 (their consumers), I10 (it sets `sent` and `failed`), TEN-007, TEN-011 and TEN-015. Numbered DEC-165 on 2026-10-29: `main` tops at DEC-161, the TEN-007, TEN-008 and TEN-009 branches hold DEC-163, DEC-162 and DEC-164.

1. **The I04 framework does not bind a tenant, so the consumers do (lesson L153 item 4, DEC-149 item 7).** `IdempotentConsumer` opened its unit of work with nothing bound, and `to_bus_message` dropped the `tenantId` application property the bus adapter sends (DEC-130 item 7), so no consumer could know its tenant. Now `to_bus_message` copies the property into `BusMessage.tenant_id` (text or bytes key; a value that is not text is no tenant), and a new `TenantBoundConsumer(inner, tenants, observe)` wraps a consumer: it dead-letters, with one fixed reason each and no tenant id in it, a message with no tenant (`message has no tenant`), a tenant that is not a valid tenant id (a network id `net-...` included: `message tenant is not valid`) and a tenant the directory does not list as active (`message tenant is unknown or not active`; a suspended tenant is not listed, so it reads the same). The inner consumer then never runs and no unit of work opens, scoped or not. A directory that cannot answer is a retry (class name only): it says nothing about the message. For a listed tenant it binds that tenant (`bind_scope`) for the whole handling of the message and restores the binding on every exit. `consumer.py` gains a `MessageConsumer` Protocol (`async handle(message) -> Outcome`) that the runner now accepts, so `IdempotentConsumer` and the wrapper are interchangeable. Every later consumer (I05, U09 and the rest) must be wrapped in `TenantBoundConsumer`; this is a known issue for I04's other users (a lesson is published). The tenant is read only from the message property, which a producer sets from a verified source (I07 from the number and account after the signature check; the outbox relay from the tenant it read the row under); a message payload field is never a tenant.
2. **The directory is `ActiveTenants`, a stand-in until TEN-007.** The wrapper asks `ActiveTenants.active_tenant_ids()` for each message (a list scan: cheap for a few tenants, to be cached when the list is long) and the entry point uses `StaticTenants` from `DIUCS_WORKER_TENANTS`. TEN-007's `container.tenants` satisfies the same Protocol, so `main` swaps `configured_tenants(os.environ)` for `container.tenants` and nothing else changes.
3. **The reply processor is not an `IdempotentConsumer`, because the use case opens its own units of work.** I04 holds one unit of work around its handler and marks the message inside it. `HandleInboundText` opens its own (a read pass, one per write, a last one for its own record), and the graph store refuses a second unit inside an open one (DEC-146 item 4, `UnitOfWorkAlreadyOpen`), so the prompt's "ReplyProcessor as an I04 handler" cannot work. `ReplyProcessor.handle(message)` holds none while the use case runs and keeps the promise in three steps: ask `processed.seen(message_id, "reply-processor")` (a duplicate if true), run the use case, then mark in its own unit of work. A crash or store failure between the run and the mark leaves no marker, the bus delivers again, and the use case answers the second run as a replay by its idempotency key and writes nothing. Two deliveries at once both run the use case (a replay, or a Conflict that is retried) and the second to mark is told the marker is held (a duplicate). Marking after the work, not before, is deliberate: a marker written first and a crash after it would lose a capacity report.
4. **`ProcessedMessages.seen(message_id, consumer) -> bool` and `Q-PROCESSED-SEEN`.** A new port method and one converted read statement (`MATCH (p:Processed {key: $key, tenantId: $tenant}) RETURN count(p) AS found`, scenario in `idempotency_store.py`, run by the generated two-tenant test). It writes nothing and uses the same length-prefixed key as `mark_if_new`, so no two pairs share a marker.
5. **The idempotency key is `sms-reply:<tenant>:<provider_message_id>`, not the bare provider id (a departure from the prompt, lesson L160).** The replay store (`Q-IDEM-*`) is unconverted, so a bare key shared by two tenants would collide and answer the second tenant a Conflict that proves the first tenant's key exists. The key is built in one function (`reply_key`) from the bound tenant, and no tenant bound is an error. TEN-011 converts the store, and the key can then be the bare id. The command has no tenant field, and none is added.
6. **Failures.** A payload that cannot be read is a `PermanentError` with a fixed text that names the field and never the value: not an `SmsReceived` message, no usable `phone_hash`, `text`, `received_at` or `provider_message_id`, a `received_at` that is not an ISO instant with an offset (a wall time is refused). `text` may be any string, a blank one included: the use case answers it. A `ValidationFailed` from the use case (a phone hash that is not a hash, for one) is permanent (`the use case refused the text as invalid`, its own text is not repeated). A `Conflict` is a retry, not a dead letter, because it can be a race with another writer that the next delivery will not meet, and the bus dead-letters after its delivery limit. Every other failure is a retry by class name. A text the use case drops (a phone that is nobody's reporter) is finished, not retried. Logs hold the message id, the outcome word and the class name only: never the text, the phone hash or the provider id.
7. **The delivery tracker is an `IdempotentConsumer` inside the wrapper**, so the bus id (`<sid>:<status>`) is marked in the same unit of work as the change and a redelivery does nothing. Its handler checks the payload (`SmsDeliveryReceived`, a provider id, a status in `queued sent delivered failed`, an error code that is absent or text; otherwise a `PermanentError` with a fixed text, so a poison receipt is dead-lettered and does not hold up the queue) and calls `set_delivery_status`. A receipt for a provider id no Communication holds is completed and dropped, not retried (a receipt can arrive before the send is recorded; another tenant's id reads the same once TEN-015 lands): the log line holds the provider id and the status. The provider's error code is logged with them for staff and is **not stored**: the Communication has no property for it (known issue; a graph-native field would be a model change).
8. **The status order lives in the store, and it is atomic.** `statuses_before(status)` (in `messaging.py`) is queued < sent < delivered and failed, which are final and neither follows the other; `received` and `grouped` are reached from nothing and never move. `Q-COMM-SET-STATUS` now takes the record's write lock first (`SET c.id = c.id`, lessons L73 and L142: the id never changes), reads the status after the lock, and writes only `WHERE c.deliveryStatus IN $movesFrom`, setting the FHIR `status` property with it (it was left `in-progress` after a delivery). `set_delivery_status` therefore returns True only when the record moved, and False for an unknown id or a refused move. A read-then-write in the tracker would have regressed under the runner's four concurrent receipts; the test holds an uncommitted `delivered` and shows a `sent` that waited does not overwrite it. I10 (which sets `sent` and `failed` after the send) gets the same rule for free: a late `sent` cannot overwrite a `delivered`.
9. **Tenant-pending, and the test that flips (TEN-015).** `Q-COMM-BY-PROVIDER` and `Q-COMM-SET-STATUS` match by provider id alone: no Communication node carries `tenantId` yet (`Q-COMM-ADD` does not stamp it, and a converted reader finds nothing the unconverted writer made, lesson L155), so until TEN-015 a receipt that arrives for tenant A can still change tenant B's Communication with the same provider id. Twilio message ids are unique across accounts, so only a forged callback signed with a tenant's own token could do it. I08 does not convert them (the whole repository is TEN-015's, with its placeholders and Concepts under TEN-008 and TEN-009). The test `test_another_tenants_message_id_reads_as_not_found_and_is_dropped` is written and marked `xfail(strict=True)`: it fails today for the reason above, and when TEN-015 converts the statements it passes, strict makes the suite fail, and TEN-015 removes the marker. Likewise the two-tenant reply test cannot seed tenant B's people and services apart (their statements are unconverted too, DEC-149 item 10): it proves what I08 owns, that each text reaches the use case under its own tenant, key and unit-of-work scope, with its own marker.
10. **The same id in two tenants.** The shared harness schema still holds the single-property marker key (until TEN-032), so the tests that put one bus id in both tenants run on `contracted_container()` (a private container with the superseded keys dropped, as the generated two-tenant test does, lesson L157); the others give each tenant its own id.
11. **The entry point.** `bootstrap/workers_main.py`: `python -m diucs.bootstrap.workers_main`. `build_runners(client, handle_inbound_text, uow_factory, tenants)` returns one `ServiceBusRunner` for each of `inbound.replies` and `inbound.receipts`, each over a `TenantBoundConsumer`; `serve(settings, tenants, stop)` opens Neo4j (`container.startup()`), Redis and Service Bus, wires `HandleInboundText` with `ReportCapacity`, `ConfirmCapacity` and a `DriverIdempotencyStore`, and runs them until stopped. The tenants come from `DIUCS_WORKER_TENANTS` (a stand-in, item 2); a missing or invalid list, or no `DIUCS_SERVICEBUS_CONNECTION`, stops the process before any connection opens with a fixed message that never repeats a value. `Neo4jConnection.driver` is added as a read-only property, byte for byte the one TEN-007 adds (so the merge is clean). `ServiceBusRunner.serve` is an alias of `run`: the architecture scan for Cypher execution reads any attribute named `run` outside the graph store, and the entry would have been refused. `serve` was not run end to end (it needs Redis, Service Bus and Neo4j together; its parts are tested), as for the relay (known issue).
12. **Trace context hook (O01).** `TenantBoundConsumer` takes `observe(message) -> context manager`, entered after the tenant is bound and left after the message is handled; the default does nothing. `BusMessage` carries no application properties yet, so O01 adds the `traceparent` property to the message and the runner, and supplies an `observe` that opens a span; no consumer changes.
13. **Binding module.** `diucs.adapters.inbound.workers.tenant_binding` is added to `BINDING_MODULES` (an edge that binds a verified tenant).
14. **Not built.** Alerting on dead-lettered inbound messages (O04); storing a receipt's error code; a retry of a receipt for an id not yet recorded (it is dropped; the send that records the id comes first in practice); the tenant directory itself (TEN-007); converting the Communication, person and idempotency statements (TEN-015, TEN-010, TEN-011).

Tests: `backend/tests/unit/adapters/inbound/workers/test_tenant_binding.py`, `test_reply_processor.py`, `test_delivery_tracker.py`, `test_servicebus_runner.py`, `backend/tests/unit/application/ports/outbound/test_delivery_order.py`, `backend/tests/unit/bootstrap/test_workers_main.py`, `backend/tests/integration/adapters/inbound/workers/test_reply_processor.py`, `test_delivery_tracker.py`, `test_inbound_two_tenants.py`, `backend/tests/integration/graph_store/test_communication_repository.py` and `test_idempotency_store.py`, and the generated `test_tenant_isolation.py`. Evidence: `docs/delivery/evidence/I08.md`.

## DEC-166 The missed-report ladder as built: how a ladder is found, one alert per missed report, the tenant, and the choices the prompt leaves open (U06)
Status: accepted (builder build-U06, under DEC-133) · Affects: U06 (`application/use_cases/missed_report_ladder.py`), U01 and U02 (`record_report` in `report_capacity.py` now stops ladders), D25 (`domain/events.py`: two new events), I05 (the consumer that runs a step), U09 (`PhoneTaskRaised` rebuilds the board), U34 (alert delivery), TEN-010, TEN-011, TEN-015 (the statements the ladder reads through), H-13 and H-27 in the hazard log. Numbers: DEC-166 was checked on 2026-10-29 against `main` (top DEC-163), `task/TEN-009-resource-store-tenant` (DEC-164) and `task/I08-reply-processor` (DEC-165); none has DEC-166.

1. **A step does what the prompt says, in one unit of work.** `MissedReportLadder.execute(LadderStepCommand(idempotency_key, actor, work_id))` handles `REMINDER`, `PHONE_TASK` and `ESCALATE_TO_LEAD`. The work is about the prompt's communication id (DEC-115 item 16), or about the service id when nobody could be texted (item 15). The reminder sends C8 (`service`, `reply_by`, `link`) to the role the prompt went to, with a fresh link token (purpose `capacity-reply`, tied to the new communication and the phone, expiring at the new reply-by) and the content sealed as U03 seals it (DEC-116); the link is never stored. The phone task is `PhoneTaskRaised {service_id, due_at, at}` on `capacity.events`; the escalation is `ReportEscalated {service_id, due_at, at}` on `alerts.events`. `due_at` is the prompt's due time (the step's time less 30, 60 or 90 minutes). Each step marks its work `done`, writes one audit entry (use case `MissedReportLadder`, naming the work, the reminder if any, and the service, never a link) and stores its result under the command key. A work that is not `scheduled` returns `ignored` and writes nothing. Result actions: `reminded`, `phone-task`, `escalated`, `stopped`, `ignored`; `LadderStepResult` also carries `communication_id` (the reminder sent, or None) and `replayed`.
2. **Constructor.** `MissedReportLadder(uow_factory, clock, ids, link_tokens, link_base_url, sealer)`. The prompt lists `idempotency` and no sealer. The sealer is needed because a `SendMessage` from the use cases of U03 carries sealed content (DEC-116 item 7, I10 opens it). `idempotency` is dropped: the early read outside the unit of work was its only use, the read inside the unit is the authoritative one, and a read outside would need the tenant from the ambient context. The tenant is not an argument: it is the scope of the unit of work (`uow.unit_scope`), refused with `TenantNotBound` when nothing, or a network, is bound. It goes into the replay key (`ladder:<tenant>:<key>`, lesson L160) and into the associated data of the sealed content. `_send_payload` and `_phone_hash` are imported from `send_prompts` (private names, so that one function builds the sealed payload and one function reads a holder's phone; renaming them is U03's).
3. **A report finds the service's ladders without a new statement.** The prompt allows `scheduled_for_service(service_id, kinds)` if the repository lacks one. It is not added. A ladder is about a communication, so a statement that joins work to its communication to its service would need `$tenant` and a scenario (DEC-142 item 5), and the `ScheduledWork` and `Communication` nodes are still written by unconverted statements (Q-WORK-ADD, Q-COMM-ADD) and carry no `tenantId`: a converted statement would find nothing, and converting those writers is TEN-015's. `stop_answered_ladders(uow, service_id, answered_at=, now=)` instead composes calls that exist: the service's own ladder (`for_about(service_id, kind)`, always with a kind, so `prompt-due` is never listed) and, for each reporter role of the service, the ladder of the latest prompt (C1, C2 or C9) sent to it. It cancels, through `cancel_work`, each `scheduled` step whose prompt due time is at or before the report's `effective_at`. **Known limit:** the ladder of an older prompt, or of a role that no longer reports for the service, is not listed. It is not left running: each step reads the figure again at its own time and stops (item 5). When TEN-015 stamps those nodes, one scoped statement can replace the composition (known-issues).
4. **`record_report` stops the ladders.** The call is in `record_report` (U01, reused by U02 and U05), after the report is stored and before the audit entry, so a number, a confirmation and an advisor-phoned figure all stop a ladder, in the unit of work that stores them. `effective_at >= due` answers a prompt, not the time the report was recorded: a figure back-dated to 11:50 does not answer the 12:00 prompt (test 5 and its back-dated form), one timed 12:00 exactly does. `prompt-due` work is left alone.
5. **A step looks again before it acts.** Order: replay check; load the work (unknown id: `NotFound`); refuse a kind that is not a ladder step (`ValidationFailed`, field `kind`); resolve the service through the communication or the work (unknown, or in another tenant: `NotFound`); take the service lock (`capacity.lock_service`, as `ReportCapacity` does); read the work again; if it is no longer `scheduled`, return `ignored`; read the latest figure and the flags. The figure is read after the lock so that a report in flight is seen, and the work is read again after it because a report that held the lock cancelled the step in its own unit. If the figure is timed at or after the due time, or the service is inactive or suspended, the step is `stopped`: its work is `done` and the other scheduled steps of the same ladder (same subject, same due time) are cancelled. A suspended or deactivated service is not chased, as U03 does not prompt it. Out of hours is not an exception: domain-rules 1.5 has none, and a missed report is chased on schedule.
6. **Time.** The step runs at `at = max(clock, work.due_at)`, so a delivery a second early is timed as the step it is. The reminder's reply-by is `at + REMINDER_REPLY_WINDOW` (30 minutes, [ASSUMED], a named constant), and the link expires then. A late step gives a full new window from when it runs.
7. **StatusChanged at the reminder.** `before` is the computed status just before the prompt's reply-by (`due + 30 min - 1 microsecond`) and `after` the status just after it (`max(at, reply-by + 1 microsecond)`), because overdue begins when the reply-by has passed (D05) and the step runs at it. The event is raised only when the two differ (a service that never reported already reads Not updated). It is on `capacity.events` with the service as session, so the board rebuilds (H-27).
8. **One alert for one missed report.** U03 gives each reporter's prompt its own ladder, so a service with two reporters has two steps at each offset. Each reporter gets their own reminder, but the advisors get one `PhoneTaskRaised`, the lead one `ReportEscalated`, and the board one `StatusChanged`, for each service and due time: a marker in the replay store (`ladder-raised:<tenant>:<what>:<service>:<due>`) is taken by the first step, and the second step is `ignored` (its work is still marked `done`, so the bus does not deliver it again). A race for the marker meets the unique key and the loser's unit is refused.
9. **Nobody to text.** A ladder about the service (no textable reporter), a role that has ended, or a holder who is missing, inactive or without a phone: no C8 is sent (`communication_id` None), the status change and the later steps still run, and the result is still `reminded`. The lead still gets the +90 step (H-13).
10. **Events.** `PhoneTaskRaised` and `ReportEscalated` are added to `domain/events.py` (fields `service_id`, `due_at`, `at`, all UTC), to the `DomainEvent` union, the topic table (`capacity.events`, `alerts.events`) and the decoder table (lesson L53). `PhoneTaskRaised` has the service as its session id (it is read in order with the report that stops it); `ReportEscalated` has none. `_when` and `_require_utc` take a field name. The board projector already rebuilds on the name `PhoneTaskRaised` (lesson L129).
11. **For I05.** Bind the tenant from the message with `TenantBoundConsumer` (lesson L165 item 1 (I08, DEC-165)) before the unit of work opens, build the command with `idempotency_key` = the work id from the message (the tenant is added by the use case), and an actor with the system role. `NotFound` (work or service unknown, or another tenant's) and `ValidationFailed` (not a ladder step) are not retried; a Conflict or a driver error is. There is no "not due yet" error: a step the clock thinks is early is run as at its due time (item 6), because dropping or dead-lettering a safety step is worse than a reminder a second early.
12. **Tenancy (transitional rule).** No Cypher is added and no statement leaves the ratchet, so there is no statement of this task to convert and no predicate-removal mutant to run on one. Every statement the use case reaches is tenant-pending today: `Q-WORK-GET`, `Q-WORK-SAVE`, `Q-WORK-FOR-ABOUT` (TEN-015), `Q-COMM-GET`, `Q-COMM-LATEST-PROMPT`, `Q-COMM-ADD` and its links (TEN-015), the person statements that list a service's reporter roles and read a holder (TEN-011), `Q-CAP-LOCK-SERVICE` and `Q-CAP-LATEST` (TEN-010), the service read through the resource store (TEN-009), and `Q-IDEM-*` (TEN-016). So on `main` today a step bound to tenant A that is given tenant B's work id finds B's work, communication and service, and would act on them. What the use case does itself is tenant-correct: it reads the tenant only from the unit of work (nothing bound, or a network, is `TenantNotBound`), every outbox row it writes is stamped by that unit (`Q-OUTBOX-ADD` is converted), the sealed content is bound to that tenant, and the replay and marker keys carry it. The control that stands until the statements are converted is the edge: the consumer binds the tenant from the message (lesson L165 item 1 (I08, DEC-165)) and the message carries the tenant of the unit that scheduled the work (DEC-157), so a step is run under its own tenant. The two-tenant test that a step for A given B's work id reads as `NotFound` is written now as a strict expected failure (`test_tenant_b_work_given_to_tenant_a_is_not_found_whatever_its_state`, decided here under DEC-133, the precedent being lesson L165 item 5 (I08, DEC-165)): when TEN-009 scopes the service lookup it passes, the strict marker fails the suite, and whoever lands that conversion removes the marker. Two tenants cannot share a resource id on the shared test schema until TEN-032, so the other two-tenant tests use distinct ids; the same-id, same-key case is a test to add when the statements are converted (known-issues).

## DEC-168 HealthcareService and capacity Observation endpoints: the write path, idempotency, error shapes, paging, roles and the tenant (R04)
Status: accepted (builder build-R04, under DEC-133; no owner gate) · Numbered DEC-168: main's top was DEC-166 when this was written, L01 takes DEC-167 and W07 took DEC-169 (checked on main at the merge of main into this branch) · Affects: R04 (`adapters/inbound/fhir_rest/routes_services.py`), `mapping.py`, `app.py`, `capability.py`, `ServiceRepository.get_versioned`, R07 to R09 and W-series readers of these routes, TEN-009, TEN-010, TEN-018.

1. **Files.** The prompt owns `routes_services.py` and says `mapping.py` is R04's; R05 created `mapping.py` (DEC-145 item 7) and R04 adds to it: `service_to_fhir`, `search_bundle`, `report_request_from_fhir` (returns a `ReportRequest`: the `ReportCapacityCommand` plus the measure and unit the sender named, so the route can check them), `validate_outbound`, `ucum_unit`, `API_SOURCES`, `FHIR_ID_PATTERN`. `app.py` includes the router after `$board` (so `{id}` cannot take `$board`) and calls `routes_services.register_capabilities()`. `capability.is_registered` (new, three lines) lets the registration run once per process however many apps are built. Port addition, no new Cypher: `ServiceRepository.get_versioned(service_id) -> (ServiceProfile, version) | None`, because the ETag needs the stored version and the profile does not carry it; it reads the resource once, so body and ETag cannot disagree. Recorded in `contracts.md` Additions.
2. **The write path calls the use case, never the store.** `POST /fhir/Observation` builds a `ReportCapacityCommand` and runs `ReportCapacity.execute`. Everything that decides a report stays there: the 0 to 999 range, no future time, the refusal to back-date behind a confirmed figure (DEC-140), the service lock (DEC-139), the report flags of domain-rules 2.3 raised in the same unit (U07, DEC-161), the stop of answered ladders (U06), the audit entry, the outbox messages and the durable replay record. The route checks only the shape of the request and its consistency with the service, then maps the answer. Order of checks, so that a refusal never depends on which services exist: role (404), `Idempotency-Key` (400), body shape (400), service scope (404, `ensure_can_act_for`), then the service's profile (404 for an unknown service, an inactive one or one with no profile yet, lesson L104), then the measure and unit match (400), then the use case. A `ValidationFailed` from the use case is re-raised naming the FHIR element (`value` becomes `Observation.valueQuantity.value`, `effective_at` becomes `Observation.effectiveDateTime`, any other `Observation`) with the use case's own fixed message. A `NotAllowed` or `NotFound` from the use case is the same 404 as an unknown service. A lead who sends method `app`, or a reporter who sends `advisor-phoned`, is refused by `check_may_report` and gets that 404: the route does not translate it into another answer, because the rule is the use case's (DEC-100 item 3).
3. **What the body may carry.** Exactly `resourceType`, `status` final, `code`, `focus` (one `HealthcareService/{id}`), `valueQuantity` (`value`, `unit`, `system` UCUM, `code`), `method`, `effectiveDateTime` (required, with seconds and a zone), plus `id` and `meta`, which are ignored (the server gives the id). Any other element, including `performer`, `derivedFrom`, `component`, `extension` and a tenant, is refused with 400 rather than dropped, because a sender must not believe a report was stored as sent when part of it was not; a `valueQuantity.comparator` would change the meaning of the figure. The value must be a JSON integer: `4.5`, `4.0`, `"4"` and `true` are refused. The measure code must be the service's own measure and the unit its UCUM annotation, because the use case stamps the service's measure on the report. The server sets no performer (the token carries no role id), so an API report has none and no echo text is sent.
4. **`organization`.** A tenant is the organisation (DEC-132 item 1) and a profile carries no separate organisation, so `organization=<id>` or `Organization/<id>` matches the caller's own scope (`uow.unit_scope`, the scope the edge bound) and nothing else. Another organisation's id, a network id, or no scope bound returns an empty Bundle (fails closed, identical for every id that is not the caller's). This is the only place a route reads the scope, and it reads the unit's, never the request's. The resource does not carry `providedBy`: nothing in the model yet names the organisation a client could compare.
5. **Search parameters and paging.** HealthcareService: `active` (only `true`; `false` is 400 because the port lists active services only), `service-category` (a code or `system|code`, unknown is 400), `organization`, `_count` (1 to 100, default 50) and `_offset` (0 to 10^6, default 0), sorted by name, with `total` and a relative `next` link that keeps the filters. Observation: `focus` required (`HealthcareService/{id}` or the bare id), `_sort` only `-date`, `_count` only `1`: only the latest report is available (there is no history port), so any other count is 400 rather than a silently shorter answer, which a client could read as "only one report exists". An unknown or repeated parameter is 400 (an unknown filter ignored would widen the answer); its name is never echoed. Observation responses carry `Cache-Control: no-store`: a cached figure is a stale figure.
6. **Sources.** The API carries `app` and `advisor-phoned` only (`API_SOURCES`). `text` and `link` have their own entry points and `email` and `feed` have none yet, so a report sent here cannot be labelled as one of those: provenance of a report is recorded in the audit trail and shown to leads, so the label must be true. 400 `Observation.method` otherwise.
7. **Error shapes.** All are OperationOutcome with fixed text and no patient data (DEC-086). A search or body problem is 400 `invalid` with `expression` the element (`Observation.focus`, `Observation.valueQuantity.value`) or the search parameter name (`focus`, `_count`), and `parameters` for an unknown one. `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` on `/fhir/Observation/{id}` are 405 `not-supported` with "Reports are not edited. Send a new report." and `Allow: GET, HEAD`, whatever the id and the caller. A missing key is 400 `required`; the cached repeat with another body is 422 and the stored repeat with another body is 409 (R03, P15). An outgoing resource or Bundle that is not valid R4B is a 500 with the class name only logged.
8. **Roles.** Services: any authenticated role reads and searches (the prompt). Observation create: `reporter` for their own services (`ensure_can_act_for`) or `lead`. Observation search and read: the board roles (wall, advisor, clinical, lead, exec, owner) for any service and a reporter for their own; every other role, including audit and support, gets the not-found answer, because capacity figures are not theirs to see and the answer must not tell them a figure exists. `GET /fhir/Observation/{id}` is not in the prompt; it is added because `POST` answers with `Location: /fhir/Observation/{id}` and a Location that 404s is a defect.
9. **Idempotency.** `Idempotency-Key` is required. The R03 cache name is `observation:<key>` (under `idem:<sub>:`), so one key sent to `$confirm-capacity` and here is not answered from the other's response. The use case receives the raw key; its durable store holds after the cache is lost (a repeat of the same report after a restart returns the same Observation, 201), and refuses the key for any other command (Conflict, 409; DEC-112 item 6). A refused request is not cached, so it can be sent again corrected.
10. **Tenancy (transitional rule).** No tenant is read, accepted or passed: not from the body, a header or a query (tests send a tenant in all three and it is ignored or refused), and no tenant text is in any response. The tenant is the unit of work's scope. Until the REST edge binds it from the token (TEN-018) the route does what R05 does: it takes the unit of work as the container gives it; TEN-018 binds the scope in `current_actor` and nothing here changes. No Cypher is added and nothing leaves the ratchet. The statements the routes reach are tenant-pending and listed in `docs/delivery/evidence/R04.md`; the two-tenant route tests are in `test_routes_services_tenants.py`: they were strict expected failures until TEN-009 landed (it scopes the resource store, so another tenant's service and report ids read as the same 404), and are plain tests now that main has it.
11. **Known duplicate.** `UnitOfWorkIdempotency` here is the same small class as `_UnitOfWorkIdempotency` in `routes_board.py` (R05), which this task does not own; unify them in `concurrency.py` when either file is next touched.


## DEC-169 Wall board variants: over capacity, out of hours, pending and the pressure banner (W07)
Status: accepted (builder build-W07, under DEC-133; no owner gate) · Numbered DEC-169: main's top decision is DEC-166, other branches hold DEC-164, DEC-167 and DEC-168; re-check main before merging. Affects: W07 (`components/board/{Tile,PressureBanner,Board}.tsx`, `Tile.module.css`, `lib/board/{format,parse}.ts`), W06's Last known rule, W08, W40, hazards H-04, H-20, H-40. Refines DEC-151 item 7 (the minimal over capacity and out of hours tiles) and DEC-152 item 6.

1. **Over capacity** is as the prompt and the "Main" and "BoardSurge" artboards say: badge word and diamond, a 3px `--c-surge` border, `+N` from `overBy` (or used minus established when `overBy` is missing, or "?" and "Phone to confirm" when neither is known), the back end's `unitLabel` as sent, "Used 14 of 12", a striped purple bar full at 100%, the comment as the meta line. Nothing changed from W05 except the pending part (item 4).
2. **Out of hours** replaces DEC-151 item 7 (no number, "Outside opening hours"): badge word "Out of hours" with the moon shape, the `#E9EDEF` background and `--c-closed` border, a big "0", the unit as sent, the meta line "Reopens HH:MM" (London time of `nextDueAt`; " tomorrow" or the weekday when that is not the same London day, the same rule as "next due"; no meta line when the back end sends no `nextDueAt`), the bar label "Out of hours" with the bar full, and the age line "Closed overnight" (the prompt's wording; it is the only line a closed service has, so no "Updated" or "next due" shows). The tile's own comment is not shown: it may describe hours that no longer apply ("Admissions until 06:00"). The "0" is always 0, whatever free count the back end held when the service closed, so a closed service never shows a number that could be read as places. It is told apart from Not accepting by its word and shape, not by colour (both are grey).
3. **"Closed overnight" is the prompt's fixed wording** and is shown for every out-of-hours service, also for a daytime closure (a lunchtime gap). The meta line beside it ("Reopens 14:00") carries the time, so the wording is loose, not unsafe. Recorded in known-issues; a later task can word it from the opening hours when the board carries them.
4. **Pending** (domain-rules 1.6): when `pending > 0` a chip "N pending" (a bordered chip with the words, so it needs no colour) shows directly after the big number, and " · N pending" is added to the bar label ("Used 4 of 8 · 1 pending", "Out of hours · 1 pending", "Used ? of 10 · 1 pending"). The big number is never reduced by it. It shows on every current tile, including Not updated and Out of hours: a request that is still open is a fact the colleagues need so that nobody books twice (H-04). "pending" is never pluralised. When it is 0 no chip and no suffix show.
5. **Last known is never softened by a variant (DEC-152).** A Last known tile shows no pending chip and no pending suffix (the count is as old as the figures and the tile must not look as if any of it were current), no "Reopens", no "Closed overnight", no status word and no comment; an Out of hours claim is still not repeated (it shows "?" and "Phone to confirm"); an over capacity figure stays "+N" as last reported. While the board is Last known the pressure banner is not shown: a pressure claim built from old figures must not stand beside the Last known banner as if it were current, and the Last known banner is then the only banner. Tests: `Tile.test.tsx` ("never carries a variant into Last known"), `Board.test.tsx`, `LiveBoard.test.tsx`, `page.test.tsx`, `e2e/variants.spec.ts` (a surge board that goes stale).
6. **The pressure banner** (`components/board/PressureBanner.tsx`, the `Banner` component with tone warning, `data-el="WALL-PRESSURE-BANNER"`): shown above the grid, below the Last known banner or the "Live updates paused" line, when the back end's `allLimitedOrWorse` is true. The flag decides, not the statuses the page can see (one source of truth: the back end's rule, domain-rules 1.7). Title "System under pressure"; text "All N services are limited, not accepting or over capacity." where N is the number of entries that are not Out of hours. Two cases the prompt does not give: N = 1 reads "The only service in hours is limited, not accepting or over capacity." (not "All 1 services"), and a true flag with no service in hours shows no banner (it would say "All 0 services"). The words carry the meaning; the warning colour only adds to them. The `Banner` warning tone is an alert, so it is announced when it first appears; it stays mounted while the board refreshes, so it is not announced again each minute.
7. **A change to the pressure level reaches the wall with the next event or the 60 second poll.** R06 pushes no event for a whole-board change with no service id (DEC-111 item 2); the front end already refetches the whole board on every event and every 60 seconds (DEC-152), so the banner can be up to a minute late. This is the known-issues row from W06; nothing more is built here.
8. **The wall refuses a structured foreign-organisation or tenant part (DEC-130, DEC-132, the W07 tenancy amendment).** The wall renders no per-entry organisation or tenant part. In addition, `parseBoardParameters` now refuses (fixed text naming the part, never the value) an entry that carries `tenantId` or `sourceTenantId`, and an entry whose `organisation` part is not the board's own top-level `organisation` (or when the board names none). The board then reads as unreadable: the first load shows Board unavailable and a refetch shows Last known, so a payload whose entry carries a foreign structured part is loud, never shown and never counted in the banner. This guard checks those structured parts only. Free text (a comment, a service name) and identifiers that embed another organisation's name are not checked and are rendered as the back end sends them; a service id goes only into `data-service-id`. The back end is the control that sends only the board's own services: tenant isolation is not yet enforced there: the service and capacity reads are unconverted until TEN-010, so this is a promise the back end does not yet keep (known-issues, W07; trigger TEN-010 and TEN-032). The back end must never send either; the network board (after M1) will read and label them and will replace this guard. This changes `lib/board/parse.ts`, which is outside the prompt's file list, because the guard cannot sit in a component that only receives parsed data.
9. **No new colour.** The pending chip uses `--c-ink` on white (`Canvas`) with a 2px border; the out-of-hours tile reuses `--tile-closed-bg` and `--c-closed`. A test reads the shipped colours and checks the chip text at 4.5:1 and the out-of-hours number at 3:1.
10. **Layout.** The tile's figure row wraps, so on a narrow tile the chip and the unit text move below the number instead of overflowing. At 1920 by 1080 the surge board is about 50 px taller than the screen because of the banner: every tile and the banner are in view, and only the key and the footer line slip below the fold (known-issues).
11. **Files outside the prompt's list.** `components/board/Board.tsx`, `lib/board/{format,parse}.ts`, `test/fixtures/board.ts`, `test/msw/handlers/board.ts`, `e2e/support/{backend,tokens}.ts`, `e2e/variants.spec.ts`, `docs/spec/contracts.md`.
12. **Not built.** Exec pressure levels normal/watch/high (W40); the network variant of the board (after M1: the banner and the out-of-hours tiles must then be computed over the projected services, with each tile labelled by its owning organisation); a status-change announcement (DEC-152 item 8).

## DEC-167 The capacity link API (L01): the tenant from the host, a scoped link token, one answer per link by its replay key, one answer to every failure, and the choices the prompt leaves open
Status: accepted (builder build-L01, under DEC-133; no owner gate) · Numbered DEC-167: main's top was DEC-166 and `task/TEN-009-resource-store-tenant` holds DEC-164 (checked on 2026-10-29 with `git show <branch>:docs/delivery/decisions.md | grep '^## DEC-'`); renumber if another branch has since taken it. Affects: L01 (`application/use_cases/link_access.py`, `adapters/inbound/link_pages/capacity_links.py`), the four link-token statements (`graph_store/link_token_repository.py`, off the ratchet), `fhir_rest/app.py` (mounts the router), W04 (the page), L02 (booking links reuse the registry), I05 (the link base URL), H-31 and H-32. Overrides the prompt's "Task-specific change (from the tenancy audit)" where it differs, and refines DEC-134 items 3 and 9.

1. **The tenant comes from the host, through the tenant directory, and from nowhere else (DEC-134 item 3).** The prompt's audit note asks for a global read of the token hash that yields the tenant. DEC-134 item 3, which says the tenant for any unauthenticated request, link pages included, comes from the host, is followed instead, and no global statement is added (DEC-163 item 2). The route reads `request.url.hostname` (no port, lower case), asks `container.tenants.by_host`, accepts only a tenant whose status is `active`, and binds it once with `bind_tenant` for the whole request. A host the directory does not know, a tenant that is not active, and a record the directory refuses (`TenantRecordInvalid`) all answer as an unknown link. Nothing in the path, query string, body or any other header is read as a tenant: a body that names one (or any field the page does not take) is refused with 400. The host only chooses where to look: a forged Host header names a tenant whose scoped statements then have to find the 128-bit token, which they cannot do for another tenant's link. **The link base URL of a prompt must therefore be the tenant's own host** (`https://<host>/l/<token>`, DEC-134 item 3): I05's composition builds `SendPrompts(link_base_url=...)` per tenant, and a renewed link is built from the verified host of the request (`RenewLinkCommand.link_base_url`, never from the body). The lead's brief speaks of a sealed token carrying the tenant in its associated data: the sealing (DEC-116) is of the stored message text, with the outbox message id, the tenant and the recipient role as associated data; the link token itself is 23 random letters (DEC-154) and carries nothing, so there is no sealed token to open.
2. **A link token is the tenant's: the four `Q-LINK-*` statements are converted.** Another tenant's link is "not found" only if the lookup is scoped, and a use case cannot check the tenant of a record the statement did not filter, so `Q-LINK-ADD`, `-GET`, `-MARK-USED` and `-BURN-KEY` now write `tenantId: $tenant` on the node and match it, each with a scenario, and leave the ratchet (101 to 97). The hash stays globally unique (`link_token_hash`, DEC-131 item 5; TEN-005), so a second tenant that stores the same hash is refused (`Conflict`), and the scenarios use `Unique` for it. LinkToken nodes written before this change carry no `tenantId` and are not found: development data only (DEC-134 item 11; `backfill_default_tenant` of TEN-005 stamps them). The pairing flows of U10 hash a tenant into the text they store and keep working unchanged.
3. **One answer to every failure.** An unknown, malformed (not URL-safe, or over 64 characters), another tenant's, wrong-purpose, dead (service no longer active, role ended, phone held by two people, prompt gone) or past-reply-by link is `410 {"state": "expired"}`; a link that has been answered is `410 {"state": "used"}`. The prompt's own tests ask for both words (used before expired, as `check_link` has it), so "used" is the one distinction a link gives, to the holder of a valid token; nothing tells an unknown link from another tenant's from an expired one, in body, status or headers (a test compares bytes). A POST with a missing or wrong CSRF token is `403 {"state":"forbidden"}` whether or not the link exists, because the CSRF token is checked from the token text alone (HMAC-SHA256 of the token hash with the secret `link-csrf`, constant-time compare, the prompt's definition) before anything is read; a host the directory does not know answers a POST the same way. A body that is not a valid answer is `400 {"state":"invalid"}`, an unconfigured app and any unexpected failure a fixed `500 {"state":"error"}`. Every response is `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, because the token is in the URL. Not hidden: the timing of a hit and a miss, and the used state to the token's holder.
4. **The page's shapes, as built.** `GET` returns `{state: "ok", purpose, serviceName, unitLabel, recordedValue, asOf, usualMin, usualMax, replyBy, nextDue, csrfToken}` (the prompt's; W04's prompt describes another shape, `open`, `usualRange`, `recordedAt`, `expiresAt`, `nextDueAt`, and says to follow L01: W04 follows this one). `purpose` is the stored purpose, `capacity-reply` (the prompt's text says `capacity-prompt`; U03 and U06 issue `capacity-reply`), and the registry is keyed by it, so L02 registers `booking-request` and `booking-change` as further `LinkPurposeHandler`s with `view`, `respond` and `renew`. Times are ISO 8601 UTC with a `Z`, to the second. `POST` success is `{serviceName, value, unitLabel, recordedAt, nextDue}`; `422 {state: "out-of-range", usualMin, usualMax}`; a Y that cannot be used is `409 {state: "send-number", reason, message: "Please send the number"}` with `reason` one of `no-figure`, `limit`, `stale`, `changed`. A refusal (422, 409, 400, 403) records nothing and burns nothing: the link stays open, so the reporter can send the number. The body takes `action`, `value` and `confirmOutOfRange` only; a figure is a whole JSON number from 0 to 999 (a float, a string or a boolean is 400), a figure is refused with `confirm` and `closed`, `confirmOutOfRange` with `confirm`.
5. **A link answer is a text answer.** The reply policy (D11, `decide_capacity_reply`) judges it with the link as the prompt (open until `expires_at`) and `confirmOutOfRange: true` as "the same figure sent again", so an out-of-range figure sent with it is recorded with the flag `out-of-range-twice` (U07, one open flag per service and reason) and an in-range one is not flagged; the figure goes through `ReportCapacity` (source `link`, the role the prompt was sent to as performer) or `ConfirmCapacity`, which write the report, status events, audit entry and idempotency record in one unit of work, and the two-Ys limit is the policy's. `closed` is the figure 0 and is judged like any figure (a service whose usual range starts above 0 must confirm it). Hazards H-31 and H-32 apply as for a Y by text (DEC-148 items 2, 17, 20): a Y is refused (`stale`) when the figure was more than 2 hours old at the moment the prompt was sent or a number has been written since the prompt (the record order, `recorded_since_prompt`), and `ConfirmCapacity` is given `expected_latest_id` so a report that lands while the Y is judged is refused (`changed`). `number_after_prompt` repeats the private test of `HandleInboundText` over the same public functions (a known issue: one shared function). The `CONFIRM_PROCESSING_LIMIT` of a text does not apply: a link is answered at once. The echo (C3) is for a text only, so a link sends none.
6. **Once, by the replay key, not by the burn.** The prompt says the token is burned in the unit of work that writes the figure. A use case opens its own unit of work and the graph store refuses a second inside it (DEC-146 item 4), so that cannot be done without changing U01 and U02. Single use is instead decided in the unit that writes the figure: the use case's replay key is `link:<tenant>:<token hash>` (the tenant is in it because `Q-IDEM-*` is unconverted, L160), stored with the report. A second, different answer finds another stored result and is refused as `Conflict` (answered `used`) with nothing written, however two requests interleave (a test runs two at once: one report, one `used`); the same answer sent at once twice replays; a link whose key is stored reads as `used` in every use case from then on; and the token is burned (`usedAt`, `burnKey`) right after the figure is stored. A failure between the two leaves the figure recorded and the link used, never open for a second answer (tested with a burn that fails). A reply lost after the burn is a `used` page to the reporter, whose copy says they will find the figure on the board (W04).
7. **Renewal.** `POST /links/{token}/renew` is `202 {"state":"accepted"}` for every token, host and body. A fresh prompt (C1, or C2 when the service has no figure and a readable window) is queued, with a new link, a Communication, an audit entry (`RenewLink`, actor channel `link`) and the replay record `renew:<tenant>:<hash>`, all in one unit of work, only if the link exists in this tenant, has expired (not used, not open), is the role's latest link-carrying prompt (C1, C2 or C8), the service is active and not suspended, the phone still holds the role, and it has not been renewed. Out-of-hours is not a reason to refuse: the reporter asked. The prompt is worded and sealed by U04's own `_render` and `_send_payload` (imported), for this tenant and role.
8. **Rate limits ([ASSUMED], domain-rules 7, named constants in `link_access.py`, kept in the cache, every key built in one place and carrying the tenant).** One tenant: 60 link requests a minute. One address: 20 requests in 10 minutes that find no link or fail the CSRF check (a link that exists gives its slot back, so a good link never costs one, and the address is hashed before it reaches the cache). One tenant: 20 renewals in 10 minutes, a slot given back when nothing was queued (an unknown or no-op renewal costs none). Over a limit: `429 {"state":"rate-limited"}` with `Retry-After`. The renewal's 429 is the one case of the prompt's "always 202": a text costs money and a limit that answered 202 would hide it. The address is `request.client.host`: behind a proxy the process must be started so that it is the client's (uvicorn `--proxy-headers` with the proxy trusted), or the 20 is shared (deployment note). A cache that cannot be reached raises and the request is refused.
9. **No secret in a response, a log or a record.** The access log of the server writes the URL: `RedactLinkTokens` is a log filter on `uvicorn.access` (installed when the module is imported) that writes `/links/[token]`. The module logs only fixed reason words; a test captures every log record of a full session of requests and finds no token, hash, CSRF token, figure or address. No node but the LinkToken's holds a token, hash or CSRF token (a test scans every property of every other node). A request body is read in pieces and abandoned at 1,024 bytes.
10. **Tenancy.** The tenant is bound by the edge only (item 1); the use cases read it from the unit of work (`TenantNotBound` if none, or a network). The statements added or changed are the four of item 2, each converted. What is still tenant-pending, listed in the evidence: the reads of the Communication, the service, the people, the capacity and the flags (`Q-COMM-*`, `Q-CAP-*`, the resource store, `Q-PERSON-*`, `Q-FLAG-*`) and the replay statements (`Q-IDEM-*`) stay unconverted, so what protects another tenant's service from an A-side link is that a link is found only in its own tenant and carries ids of its own tenant's records (item 2). Cross-scope reads this task would need: none (a link concerns one tenant's one service).
11. **Not built, and where it goes.** The Next.js page (W04), booking links (L02), the process that serves the app and sets `app.state.link_pages` and the per-tenant link base URL in the prompt jobs (I05 and the serving entry point), removal of expired link tokens (a retention sweep, known-issues).

Tests: `backend/tests/unit/application/use_cases/test_link_access.py`, `backend/tests/unit/adapters/inbound/link_pages/test_capacity_links.py`, `backend/tests/integration/application/test_link_access.py` and `test_link_access_tenants.py`, `backend/tests/integration/adapters/inbound/link_pages/test_capacity_links.py` and `test_capacity_links_tenants.py`, `backend/tests/integration/graph_store/test_link_token_repository.py` and the generated `test_tenant_isolation.py`. Evidence: `docs/delivery/evidence/L01.md`.

## DEC-172 The capacity link pages (W04): the read through the BFF, the host forwarded to the back end, the shapes as L01 built them, and the wording the prompt leaves open
Status: accepted (builder build-W04, under DEC-133; no owner gate) · Numbered DEC-172: main's top was DEC-169, and branches hold DEC-170 (TEN-010, TEN-011) and DEC-171 (TEN-015) (checked on 2026-10-29 with `git show <branch>:docs/delivery/decisions.md | grep '^## DEC-'`); renumber if another branch has since taken it. Affects: W04 (`app/l/[token]/`, `app/api/bff/links/[token]/`, `components/reporter/`, `lib/links/`), L02 (the booking page the redirect names), W09 (the `/sign-in` link), H-41, DEC-167 (its shapes), DEC-134 item 3 (the host).

1. **The page reads the link through its own BFF, from the browser.** The server component (`app/l/[token]/page.tsx`) checks the token's shape and renders `LinkLoader`, a client component that calls `GET /api/bff/links/[token]` once. Two reasons. Next.js allows cookie writes only in Server Actions and Route Handlers, so a server page cannot set the link's CSRF cookie (item 3). And a server read plus a browser read would make two back-end reads per view, against the 60 link requests a minute that a tenant gets (DEC-167 item 8): forty prompts sent at one time would then exhaust the budget and show "could not load" to reporters. Cost: the page shows "Opening your link…" for one round trip before content. Not a server-rendered first paint.
2. **The back end's host is the browser's host.** The BFF reads the request's `Host` (or its own URL's host when the header is absent) and sends it to the back end as `Host`, because the back end picks the tenant from the host (DEC-167 item 1). The global `fetch` of Node ignores a `Host` header, so `lib/links/server.ts` calls `node:http` (the default import, so a test double intercepts it). `DIUCS_FHIR_BASE_URL` must end in `/fhir`; the link routes are at its origin. Nothing in the body, the query or any other header picks a tenant.
3. **CSRF.** The BFF GET sets `diucs_link_csrf` to the link's CSRF token (the back end's HMAC, DEC-167 item 3), HttpOnly, SameSite Strict, path `/api/bff/links/<token>` (so two links in one browser do not collide), one hour. The page gets its copy of the value from the BFF's JSON answer. A POST must send `X-CSRF-Token` equal to that cookie (constant-time), or it is 403 before anything is forwarded; the back end then checks the value against the link. `renew` has no CSRF check: the back end answers 202 for every token, the token is the capability, and a forged request cannot know it.
4. **The shapes are L01's, not the prompt's** (the prompt says to follow L01 where they differ). GET 200 is `{state: "ok", purpose: "capacity-reply", serviceName, unitLabel, recordedValue, asOf, usualMin, usualMax, replyBy, nextDue, csrfToken}`; the page reads `replyBy` as "expires at" and `asOf` as "as of". POST 200 is `{serviceName, value, unitLabel, recordedAt, nextDue}`. The out-of-range refusal is **422** `{state: "out-of-range", usualMin, usualMax}` (the prompt says 409 with `code`); a refused confirm is 409 `{state: "send-number", reason, message}`. A 410 carries **no time** (the prompt's `closedAt` is not in L01), so the expired page cannot say when the link closed. A rate limit is 429 with `Retry-After`, shown as "Too many tries". The BFF forwards only `action`, `value` and `confirmOutOfRange` from the body, so nothing else (a tenant, for one) reaches the back end; an invalid body is 400 before the back end is called.
5. **One message for expired, used and unknown.** The 410 from the back end is the same page whatever its state word, and the page renders the same words for all three (a test compares the text word for word, and the browser test compares the page for an expired and an unknown link). The copy is "This link has expired", "This link can no longer be used.", "Or reply to the text message instead.", "A link works once. If you already sent your update, you will find it on the board." A back-end outage is a different message ("We could not load this link. Try again in a few minutes."), so it is never read as expiry.
6. **The unit is shown as the back end sends it** (`unitLabel`, for example "referrals in the next 2 hrs"), so the link says the same as the text the reporter got. The prompt's "2 hours" wording is not used. The question is built from the unit by splitting at " in " (`splitUnitLabel`): "How many referrals can you take in the next 2 hrs?", the stepper label "Referrals in the next 2 hrs", the hint "referrals · usual range 0 to 8". The footer says "No login." only when a figure is on record, as the prompt's two footers do.
7. **Out of range.** A figure outside the usual range gets the prompt's message ("That is outside your usual range of 0 to 8. Check it and press Send new number again to confirm."). The page keeps that figure flagged: sending it again sends `confirmOutOfRange: true`, and changing the figure clears the flag. The back end records it with the `out-of-range-twice` flag (DEC-167 item 5).
8. **Other refusals.** 409 send-number shows "Please send the number."; 429 "Too many tries. Wait a few minutes, then try again."; any other failure "We could not record that. Try again."; a new link after expiry that is refused for its budget shows "Too many new links. Wait a few minutes, then try again.", and one that failed shows "We could not send a new link. Try again.". A 410 on a press switches the page to the expired message at once.
9. **The thank-you page** (`/l/[token]/thanks`) takes its answer from the address the link page sends it to: service name, figure, unit, recorded time and next update (London time to the minute). The address never holds the token. The page validates each value (a whole figure from 0 to 999, a valid instant, names of at most 120 characters); anything else shows "Thank you" with no figure. "See the live board" links to `/sign-in`, the staff sign-in that W09 builds; until then that link is not found. The prompt's "Something wrong? Change it" is not built (the correction window is out of scope).
10. **Booking links** (a purpose that starts with `booking`) go to `/l/[token]/booking` by a client-side replace. L02 builds that page.
11. **Privacy of the page.** The page loads nothing from another origin (its fonts are self-hosted by `next/font`; no external script or image). It sends `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and `robots` noindex in its metadata, and is dynamic (never cached). Nothing it does logs a token, a figure, a URL or an address. The Next server's own access log writes the page path, which holds the token: that is a deployment matter (known-issues, W04).
12. **The button** (`components/ui/Button.tsx`, a W03 file) gets an additive `disabled` prop, so "Choose a number to send" is disabled without the busy state (`aria-busy` means work is in progress). No other W03 behaviour changes.
13. **Hazard H-41.** Its controls are verified by the W04 tests listed in the hazard log. No new hazard: the risks are H-41's (a token or a figure leaked, a link that works for a stranger, a page that tells links apart).

Tests: `lib/links/{model,server,csrf}.test.ts`, `app/api/bff/links/[token]/{route,renew/route}.test.ts`, `app/l/[token]/{page,thanks/page}.test.tsx`, `components/reporter/{LinkLoader,CapacityResponder,LinkExpired}.test.tsx`, `components/ui/Button.disabled.test.tsx`, and the browser tests `e2e/links.spec.ts` (390 CSS px and the 320 CSS px reflow). Evidence: `docs/delivery/evidence/W04.md`.

## DEC-170 The person, registration and scope-list statements are tenant-scoped (TEN-011, refines DEC-130 items 1 to 3, DEC-134 item 1 and DEC-150 item 10)
Status: accepted (builder build-TEN-011, under DEC-133; no owner gate) · Numbered DEC-170: main's top was DEC-169 when this was written (checked on 2026-10-29 with `grep '^## DEC-' docs/delivery/decisions.md` on main); TEN-010 and TEN-015 hold DEC-167 to DEC-169 on their branches. Re-check main at the merge. Affects: `adapters/outbound/graph_store/person_repository.py`, `registration_repository.py`, `scope_list_repository.py`, `scenario.py` (`SeedRel.props`), `tests/support/tenant_seed.py` (seeds a relationship's properties), `unconverted.py` (nineteen ids leave), `tests/unit/adapters/outbound/graph_store/test_queries.py` (cap 97 to 78), `test_tenant_ratchet.py`, `tests/integration/graph_store/test_person_scope_tenants.py` (new), `test_tenancy.py`, `test_scope_list_repository.py`, `test_person_round2.py`.

1. **Nineteen statements, each tenant-scoped on every node it matches, merges or creates, each with a scenario.** Person (8): `Q-PERSON-PHONE-FIND`, `Q-PERSON-ROLES-OF`, `Q-PERSON-SET-PROPS`, `Q-PHONE-SERVICES-HELD`, `Q-PHONE-SERVICES-AT`, `Q-SERVICE-REPORTER-ROLES`, `Q-ROLE-CHANNEL`, `Q-ROLE-COVER`. Registration (6): `Q-REG-BY-STATUS`, `Q-REG-FOR-SERVICE`, `Q-REG-SET-PROPS`, `Q-REG-DRAFT-CLEAR`, `Q-REG-DRAFT-ADD`, `Q-REG-DRAFT-FOR`. Scope list (5): `Q-SCOPE-ENSURE-LIST`, `Q-SCOPE-LOCK-LIST`, `Q-SCOPE-UPSERT-ENTRY`, `Q-SCOPE-ENTRIES`, `Q-SCOPE-ENTRY-FOR`. The ids leave the ratchet in the same commit, and the cap in `test_queries.py` falls from 97 to 78. The `Q-PROV-*` statements are the audit's (TEN-017) and the `Q-IDEM-*` statements are the idempotency bundle (TEN-016), not this one.
2. **The phone lookup is one tenant's.** `Q-PERSON-PHONE-FIND` and the two service-of-phone statements match the phone within the bound tenant. The same phone held by practitioners of two tenants is found once in each, so it is not a cross-tenant `Conflict`. `Conflict` remains for two active practitioners of one tenant on one phone (DEC-065), which is intended. The webhook tests that TEN-009 weakened are restored (`test_tenancy.py`): the same sender is a reporter of both tenants and each tenant's text goes to its own queue, and a sender known only to the other tenant is unknown here (nothing queued, no borrowed reporter).
3. **The role channel matches the role first.** `Q-ROLE-CHANNEL` matches the role in the tenant, then merges the text, email or push `Concept` in the tenant, then creates the `CHANNEL` relationship. A role that is not there creates no `Concept` (the prior text merged the concept before the match, so a missing role left one behind). A channel never links to another tenant's concept.
4. **A cover joins the tenant's practitioner only.** `Q-ROLE-COVER` matches the role and the covering practitioner in the tenant. A covering practitioner of the other tenant is `NotFound`, as `save_role` already refused it through the store's scoped check.
5. **One scope list per tenant.** `Q-SCOPE-ENSURE-LIST` merges on `id` and `tenantId`; the composite key `tenant_resource_id` (TEN-005) backs the refusal of a racing first write (L90). The lock, the upsert and the two reads match the tenant's list and the tenant's service only, so an entry cannot name another tenant's service.
6. **Drafts and registrations are the tenant's.** The draft rows match their own tenant's task, and every draft row a save creates carries the tenant. The registration statements match the tenant's task, service and codes.
7. **Scenarios may give a relationship properties.** `SeedRel.props` is seeded by `seed_statement` (the cover's `until`, the scope entry's `flag`). A relationship carries no tenant, because it joins nodes of one tenant (DEC-130 item 1, and the invariant test). `validate_scenario` refuses a property name that is not a plain identifier, and a reserved name (`tenantId`, `seedMarker`) on a relationship.
8. **Not built here.** The `accountRef` lookup that `tenancy-plan.md` names for TEN-011 is not in the code (no statement reads an account reference from a practitioner or a role), so there is nothing to scope. `Q-SCOPE-ENSURE-LIST` still creates the list without a `key`, as it did before (known-issues, TEN-011).
9. **Caller tests the change forces.** `test_scope_list_repository.py` writes its list and entry with the tenant it binds; `test_person_round2.py` matches the stamped role; the webhook tests seed the second reporter in tenant B with the sender the test uses.

Tests: `backend/tests/integration/graph_store/test_person_scope_tenants.py` (two tenants on a private container, the same keys in both), the generated `test_tenant_isolation.py` (each of the nineteen runs as A and as B, and the predicate-removal mutant of each fails it), `backend/tests/integration/adapters/inbound/sms_webhook/test_tenancy.py`, `backend/tests/unit/adapters/outbound/graph_store/test_tenant_ratchet.py` and `test_queries.py`. ## DEC-171 The communication and scheduled-work statements are tenant-scoped (TEN-015, reworks P07 and P08)

Status: accepted (builder build-TEN-015, under DEC-133; no owner gate) · Numbered DEC-171: main's top decision is DEC-169 and the TEN-010 and TEN-011 branches each hold DEC-170 (both are still open); re-check main and every open branch before merging, and renumber this one if another lands first. Affects: `adapters/outbound/graph_store/communication_repository.py` and `scheduled_work_repository.py` (13 statements: Q-COMM-ADD, -GET, -EXISTS, -BY-PROVIDER, -SET-STATUS, -LATEST-PROMPT, -LINK-RECIPIENT, -LINK-ABOUT, -LINK-REPLY; Q-WORK-GET, -ADD, -SAVE, -FOR-ABOUT), `unconverted.py` (97 to 84 ids on this branch), `adapters/inbound/workers/delivery_tracker.py`, the I08 receipt test (strict xfail removed), `tests/integration/graph_store/test_communication_predicates.py` (new), and the caller tests of the two repositories. Evidence: `docs/delivery/evidence/TEN-015.md`.

1. **Scope.** The thirteen statements above leave the ratchet and carry a scenario each. Every node a statement matches, merges or creates carries `tenantId: $tenant`: the Communication, its topic and medium Concepts (merged by key and tenant, so they follow the composite `(tenantId, system, code)` key), the placeholder PractitionerRole and HealthcareService it links to (merged by key and tenant), the ScheduledWork and its placeholder subject. The tenant comes only from `run_query`; no statement takes it from a parameter.
2. **No LIMIT on the provider-id lookup (`Q-COMM-BY-PROVIDER`).** A Twilio message id is unique within a tenant, so the lookup returns one row. A `LIMIT 1` with no order hides another tenant's row from the generated probe, which runs each statement with the other tenant's record present, so the leak would not show in the rows. The latest-prompt statement keeps its `LIMIT 1` because its `ORDER BY` (sent time, then id) is what defines the answer; its scenario gives each tenant's prompt its own `Marked` id so the unscoped order picks the other tenant's row and the leak shows.
3. **Predicates on nodes reached through a relationship.** `_READ` (the optional matches of the topic, medium, role and service), the second node of each work match and the first node of the latest-prompt match are stamped as well, as the rule requires. Each of them is redundant under DEC-132 item 8 (a relationship joins nodes of one tenant): with the other node scoped, removing the predicate cannot change a row, so the single-occurrence mutant is equivalent. `test_communication_predicates.py` pins the nineteen such occurrences, and requires every other occurrence of the thirteen statements to be killed by the generated probe. Removing all of a statement's predicates is killed by `test_tenant_isolation.py` for every statement.
4. **I08 closed.** The strict xfail on `test_another_tenants_message_id_reads_as_not_found_and_is_dropped` is removed and the test passes: a receipt for tenant A's provider id finds nothing of tenant B's, completes, and leaves B's status as it was. This closes DEC-165 item 9 and the residual in H-39 (the hazard row is updated in this commit).
5. **Ordering with TEN-011 (dependency, not a defect of this change).** `Q-ROLE-CHANNEL` (TEN-011, unconverted on main) creates the channel Concept nodes with no tenant. The tenant-scoped merge of the medium Concept in `Q-COMM-ADD` does not find them, and the shared harness schema still holds the superseded `(system, code)` key until TEN-032, so on main alone 281 tests of `tests/integration/application` and `tests/integration/graph_store` fail with a constraint error on the channel Concept (lesson L155: the writer converts before its readers). TEN-011's branch converts `Q-ROLE-CHANNEL` (a tenant-stamped merge). This branch must merge after TEN-011, and the merged tree was run to confirm it (evidence, "Merged tree"). The merge conflicts in `unconverted.py` (none) and in the two ratchet tests (`test_queries.py` cap, `test_tenant_ratchet.py` test list) are resolved by keeping both sides and the cap that is true after both merges (65).
6. **Not built.** A single statement for a service's scheduled ladder work (U06, DEC-166 item 3): the composition in `stop_answered_ladders` stays, because it is correct and the work and communication reads it uses are now scoped. The replacement is a separate change and its known issue stays open. Operator and support reads, the audit provenance statements (`Q-PROV-*`, TEN-017) and the outbox (TEN-016) are not in this task.
